fatigue, frustration, attention, and their combinations affect BCI performance, and the underlying class distributions are sensitive to changes in these states.

fatigue and frustration are significantly correlated with BCI performance, that BCI performance varies across mental states, that there are regions in mental state where performance is more accurate, and that class distributions vary across mental states.

fatigue, frustration, attention, and their combinations are significantly related to EEG-BCI classification accuracy, and that these effects can be visualized in the form of a multivariate mental state space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how mental state can affect the performance of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and how we can design BCIs to adapt to the user’s mental state.
the relationship between user mental state and brain-computer interface (BCI) performance.
the effects of mental states (e.g. fatigue, frustration, attention) on BCI performance, and we are interested in how these mental states can be used as a basis for developing adaptive BCI systems.

mental state is an important consideration for the design of BCI applications, and that it can be measured using self-report.
